title: Cross-regional fallback burn & coverage — mini sheet
content:
Mini spreadsheet and notes for quick ops decision on cross-regional fallbacks.

Table (columns): region, primary_model, fallback_model, avg_qps, peak_qps, est_hourly_burn_usd_primary, est_hourly_burn_usd_fallback, fallback_event_rate_pct, est_coverage_pct, peak_fallback_rate_pct, recommended_action, notes

Rows: 
us-west-2, redwood-7b-int8, redwood-7b-4g-quant, 120, 420, 18.0, 9.5, 4.2, 98.6, 6.8, "Enable cross-region cache share; watch slot contention"
us-east-1, redwood-13b-q4, redwood-13b-q2, 240, 900, 72.0, 38.0, 7.1, 95.3, 9.4, "Consider temporary burst capacity for weekday peaks"
eu-west-1, redwood-13b-q2, redwood-7b-int8, 60, 180, 19.0, 9.5, 3.5, 99.1, 4.0, "Fallback only for non-low-latency routes"
asia-northeast-1, redwood-7b-int8, redwood-7b-4g-quant, 30, 120, 4.5, 2.3, 10.2, 86.7, 18.0, "High fallback rate during infra upgrade windows — schedule warning"
sa-east-1, redwood-7b-int8, redwood-7b-4g-quant, 8, 32, 1.2, 0.6, 12.5, 74.0, 22.0, "Low coverage; consider routing to us-east-1 during incidents"

Key calculations / assumptions (quick):
- est_hourly_burn_usd_primary = avg_token_rate_equiv * model_unit_cost (back-of-envelope, from Pricing sheet)
- fallback burn uses smaller model unit cost estimate (quantized variants)
- fallback_event_rate_pct measured by sampled traffic during last 7 rolling days; peak_fallback_rate_pct uses 99th-percentile hour
- est_coverage_pct = 100 - (fallback_event_rate_pct * degradation_factor) where degradation_factor tuned per region (0.6 default)

Quick summary:
- Total incremental hourly burn if fallbacks engaged at peak: ~69.9 USD across all regions (back-of-envelope).
- Regions with highest operational risk: asia-northeast-1, sa-east-1 (higher peak fallback rates and low coverage).
- Most cost-efficient fallback configuration: us-west-2 uses quantized fallback yielding ~50% burn reduction for degraded calls.

Immediate recommended actions (short list):
1) Ops: add temporary alerting for fallback_rate_pct > 10% sustained over 15m for APAC + SA clusters. (Owner: Ethan)
2) Platform: enable cross-region KV prefix cache share experiment for us-west-2 to reduce fallback frequency during spikes. (Owner: Maya)
3) Product: classify routes by latency-sensitivity so lower-latency routes avoid fallbacks where coverage < 90%. (Owner: Sofia)
4) Infra: schedule rolling infra maintenance in asia-northeast-1 outside peak request windows next 2 weeks and publish runbook. (Owner: Alexei)

Notes / open questions:
- Need to reconcile model unit costs used here with latest pricing table (pricing-sheet link in Confluence). This sheet used cached numbers from 2027-05-10.
- Is temporary cross-region routing allowed under current data residency controls? Check with security/compliance (ticket: PLAT-998).
- Fallback coverage model is heuristic; should run a 72h burn simulation with synthetic traffic to validate.

Choppy notes to self:
- If fallback_event_rate spikes during canary, throttle canary to 25% and enable image-level tracing.
- Quick ask to SRE: can we surface per-model KV hit rate for last 48h in dashboards? Will make heuristics ~x4 better.

Appendix (quick):
- Raw sample used: last7d_fallback_sample.csv (attached to JIRA INFR-4321).
- Short decompress of anomalies: 2027-05-09 03:00 UTC spike in us-east-1 due to customer A batch job; caused fallback to 12.4% for 18m.

Action log (mini):
- 2027-05-12: initial quick sheet populated by Maya (prelim numbers).
- 2027-05-13: Ethan adds alert thresholds.
- 2027-05-14: Sofia adds latency-sensitivity classification notes; in_review for wider ops sync.

Quick links: Confluence playbook + JIRA keys above; PR for cache experiment: github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/2145

End of mini sheet.
